hints: Identify what makes the substance detectable after it enters the body.
walkthrough: a substance containing radioactive nuclei that is introduced into the body and absorbed by the tissue being studied
Its emitted radiation allows its distribution to be detected.

hints: Think about the interaction between a particle and its antiparticle.
walkthrough: a particle interacting with its antiparticle so that mass is converted into energy

hints: The tracer emits a positron. Identify its antiparticle in the tissue.
walkthrough: The annihilating particles are a positron and an electron.

hints: Include the rest mass of both particles in the energy calculation.
walkthrough: The two particles each have rest mass $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}$. Their total rest energy is $E=2m_ec^2$.

hints: The two gamma photons share the released energy equally.
Use the energy of one photon in the photon-energy equation.
Consider the directions of the photon pair and how detectors identify one event.
Repeated detections locate the tracer distribution.
walkthrough: Each annihilation produces two gamma photons travelling in opposite directions. Detectors outside the body register the pair.
The line joining the detectors identifies a line on which the annihilation occurred; detection-time differences can help locate the event along it.
Combining many such events reconstructs an image of tracer concentration in the tissue.
